findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, with confusing dead logic
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` and returns false on both branches, so the result never depends on the flag. The inverted flag check and the redundant branches suggest a mistake or a half-finished edit. If SQL expressions are meant to be disabled outright, the function should be `return false`, or the check should be removed. The flag is also now meaningless, and the error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' hides the real reason (disabled for security).

findings.title: SQL command construction paths outside the reader still reachable
findings.body: Only ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery blocks SQL. UnmarshalSQLCommand (the legacy path that calls NewSQLCommand) has no guard and is not gated. It now fails with a generic 'error reading SQL command' because TablesList returns 'not implemented', hiding the real reason. The disabling is incomplete and inconsistent: it relies on stubs rather than an explicit check at all entry points.

findings.title: No tests for the disabled behavior
findings.body: No test verifies that SQL query types are rejected by the reader or that the stub DB returns errors. Existing SQL expression tests that relied on DuckDB will likely fail or remain unadjusted, and the security-critical behavior is left unprotected against regressions.
